ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banking, licensing, and each material onboarding event, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized representatives, beneficial owners, controllers, major suppliers, distributors, and relevant healthcare intermediaries against United Nations sanctions, directly applicable European Union restrictive measures, French asset-freezing lists under the Monetary and Financial Code, and applicable domestic enforcement lists. OFAC screening is mandatory for United States persons, United States-dollar or United States-financial-system exposure, and as a prudent correspondent-bank control; it is not independently binding on an otherwise non-US French transaction without a US nexus. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, family members, and known close associates; identify source of wealth and source of funds; document false-positive resolution; prohibit onboarding where sanctions exposure cannot be resolved; and maintain auditable screening records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, operated by Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI): formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; registration data recorded in the Registre National des Entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be stated in the French filing in Latin characters and must include or be compatible with the required corporate form designation, such as Société par Actions Simplifiée or SAS. French is the operative filing language. A foreign-language or transliterated name may be used if it is not misleading, is available, and complies with public-order, consumer-protection, trademark, and corporate-name rules. Registration of a company name does not create comprehensive trademark protection; separate INPI trademark clearance is required.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names confusingly similar to an existing registered company, trademark, public body, or regulated professional activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation certificate with a uniform 30-day legal validity period. Any provisional availability or draft-name hold offered by a filing intermediary or portal must be confirmed directly with INPI and must not be treated as enforceable exclusivity. Conduct RNE, trademark, domain-name, trade-name, and regulated-sector searches before filing. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the name, obtain the written reason, correct the filing or select an alternative name, and resubmit through the portal within the stated correction period. For a formal administrative decision, submit a reasoned recours gracieux to the issuing authority and, where appropriate, a recours hiérarchique or application to the competent administrative court within the applicable two-month period from notification. A name objection involving trademark infringement should be addressed separately through the INPI or judicial trademark procedure. Use of terms implying pharmaceutical manufacturing, medicinal products, or a regulated healthcare status must be validated before filing and must not misrepresent the actual license status.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France. Commercial domiciliation with an authorized domiciliation company is generally permissible for the registered office, subject to a written domiciliation agreement, documentary verification, and availability of premises for official notices and inspections. A virtual office is not an adequate substitute for premises used for manufacturing, storage, quality control, cold-chain operations, clinical or pharmaceutical activities, or regulated distribution. Botulinum-toxin formulation, filling, lyophilization, storage, and release activities require appropriately authorized and inspected physical premises, documented quality systems, qualified personnel, and applicable pharmaceutical or public-health approvals. The registered office should not be represented as the manufacturing or licensed establishment unless it satisfies those requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national probability is published. For a high-risk botulinum-toxin and medical-aesthetics business, an internal planning estimate is 15% to 30% for an unannounced or short-notice compliance visit during the first three years, with materially higher exposure after licensing, adverse intelligence, temperature-control deviations, pharmacovigilance signals, customs anomalies, or AML alerts. Regulatory inspections may be conducted by ANSM, regional health authorities, customs, tax authorities, labor authorities, or other competent bodies depending on the activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration) and L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Decree No. 84-406 of 30 March 1984 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce territorialement compétent — Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), operating through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique de formalité de création d'entreprise, accompanied by the certified or executed Articles of Association and mandated annexes for SAS incorporation (electronic CERFA-based declaration).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; the share capital is freely fixed in the Articles of Association. At incorporation, every cash subscription must be fully subscribed and paid into a blocked bank account opened in the company name 'en formation', with the deposit attested by the bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. Funds are released only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's valuation report (rapport du commissaire aux apports) unless validly waived.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the shareholders' subscription for the named number of ordinary shares comprising the capital of the SAS has been accepted and the consideration fully paid into the blocked account. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office is adopted at the address set out in the Articles of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER that the appointed President is vested with full authority to bind the company within its corporate purpose, and that the appointed General Manager is authorised for day-to-day administration. The officers accept their mandates. RESOLVED FURTHER that the President may complete RCS registration, execute all incorporation filings, apply for industrial and environmental permissions, and instruct counsel until the company is fully licensed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SAS constitutive documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel / notary (optional but recommended for share transfer restrictions and governance provisions); final validation through Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare final Articles of Association in French, including the corporate object covering fermentation and lyophilization of neurotoxin formulations, capital, registered office, duration, board powers, appointment of President, and share transfer restrictions. Obtain written consents from all officers, initial every page, date and sign the Articles and any notarized instruments if real-property contributions are present.
required_dossiers: Sheet of share subscription and payment allocation
Consent letters of President and General Manager
Shareholder identification and beneficial ownership schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies statutory defects, prepare amending resolutions or re-execute the Articles; ensure all initialled pages are replaced and re-signed before submission. If a contribution in kind triggers mandatory auditor involvement, obtain the valuation report or valid shareholder waiver.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocking of cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; verified by legal counsel before filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company 'en formation', deposit the paid-up capital, and request a certificate of blocked funds. The bank must expressly confirm that the funds are held until the RCS registration certificate is produced or a power of attorney from the incorporators allows withdrawal.
required_dossiers: Source of funds evidence if requested by bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the blocking certificate, engage another eligible bank or use the Caisse des Dépôts official sequester procedure. If the bank requests additional AML documents, provide sworn declarations of source of funds promptly; any corrected certificate must be reflected in the final filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the mandatory legal notice in a legal announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized legal announcement gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before submitting the electronic incorporation file, publish a notice containing company name, form, capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, officer names, and intended RCS registry. Obtain the official publication receipt bearing the bidding/journal reference and date.
required_dossiers: Extract of final Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal notice is incomplete or defective, publish a corrective notice within two business days and before filing. Keep both receipts and notify the registry if correction occurs after filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation dossier with Guichet Unique and RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); routed to Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique portal, select 'création de société commerciale — SAS', complete the standardized declaration, upload all required documents, certify exact data, pay the applicable state and greffe fees, and submit electronically. The system routes the dossier to the competent commercial court registry, INSEE, DGFiP and social security authorities.
required_dossiers: Signed and initialled Articles of Association PDF
Consent to office of President and General Manager
Domiciliation agreement or right-to-use registered office proof
Identity documents of shareholders, directors and beneficial owners
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is returned for correction, use the online rectification procedure within the prescribed period (generally 15 days), upload missing or corrected documents, and resubmit. If the rejection concerns the legal entity type or signature formalities, obtain the corrected signatures and re-file without substantive changes; re-publish the announcement only if the company name or capital is modified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of K-Bis, SIRET and tax/social identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce territorialement compétent; automatic interfacing with INSEE, DGFiP and URSSAF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registry verifies the completed dossier, approves the registration, assigns the RCS number and SIREN, and issues the extrait K-Bis. The greffe transmits data to INSEE for SIRET, to DGFiP for tax accounts, and to URSSAF for business registration. The company collects the official K-Bis extract and verifies the accuracy of all company details.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry and publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact the greffe via the Guichet Unique or by written request. If the K-Bis is not received after SLA, apply directly with the greffe; if tax/social identifiers are not generated, send the K-Bis copy to DGFiP and URSSAF with a demand for opening of individualized accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of mandatory corporate governance records and legal share registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel and statutory management; no separate government filing beyond the beneficial-owner register already filed at RCS.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the company statutory books or dematerialized registers, record the first board resolution, share subscriptions, capital movements, officer appointments and subsequent board decisions. Prepare the register of securities (registre de titres), share transfer book, and decision files in compliance with Article L.227-9 of the Commercial Code and tax record-keeping rules.
required_dossiers: List of officers with dated appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any governance register is defective, correct the omission through a later board or shareholders' resolution ratifying the action. If missing director declarations affect RCS data, file a modification in the RCS within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (ANSM) — Inspection and Licensing Directorate, co-operating with DREAL for site operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pharmaceutique pour la fabrication, l'importation et la libération de lots de médicaments biologiques (including botulinum toxin formulations), issued pursuant to Articles L.4211-1, L.5124-1 et seq., R.5124-2 and R.5126-3 of the French Public Health Code; supports EU Good Manufacturing Practice certification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement / Inspection des installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (Ministère de la Transition écologique).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A obligation — installation soumise à autorisation ICPE under Article L.511-1 and L.512-1 of the Environment Code; full environmental impact assessment and public inquiry required for fermentation, lyophilization and toxic biological product operations, based on installed capacity and risk potential.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the French ministerial order of 2 February 1998 on water abstraction and industrial pollutant emissions and applicable ICPE air/water discharge requirements: pH 5.5–9.5, effluent temperature below 30°C, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L; solvent VOCs contained by carbon capture or abatement; biotoxic aerosol containment by HEPA filtration; botulinum toxin process waste inactivated by validated oxidation/autoclaving before disposal; all waste tracked under Article R.541-12 of the Environment Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Production facilities must obtain a fire safety conformity certificate from the competent commission, electrical safety verification, structural load assessment for lyophilizers and cold storage vaults, ATEX zoning review, completion of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), occupational health clearance by the authorized work physician, and civil defense authorization before commencing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE); official portals: https://www.impots.gouv.fr and the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS incorporated in France files its formation and beneficial-owner information through the INPI Guichet unique. The formalities authority transmits the filing to the competent registry, INSEE and the tax administration. INSEE issues the entity SIREN and establishment SIRET identifiers. The entity requests VAT registration and activation of its professional tax account with the competent SIE through the impots.gouv.fr business portal or directly with the SIE. The French VAT number is generally the prefix FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity carrying out taxable transactions in France without a French establishment must apply to the SIEE for a French VAT number, submit constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identification of directors and beneficial owners, expected transaction details, and banking and correspondence information. A non-EU entity may generally require a French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement removes that requirement. VAT registration does not replace product, pharmaceutical, customs, controlled-substance, or medical-device authorizations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by operation of law. A qualifying SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu) for a maximum of five financial years, subject to statutory conditions, including activity and ownership requirements, non-listing, incorporation within the relevant statutory period, and prescribed employee, turnover, and balance-sheet limits. The election is made with the tax administration within the statutory deadline and is irrevocable for the elected period. France has no United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement ATAD restrictions on deduction, non-inclusion outcomes, imported mismatches, and reverse-hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée or VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, the principal VAT franchise thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods, sales for consumption on premises, and accommodation activities, and EUR 37,500 for services and non-commercial activities, subject to enhanced thresholds and legislative amendments. These thresholds concern eligibility for the franchise en base and are not a universal VAT nexus safe harbor. A French SAS may be required to register and charge VAT from the first taxable transaction if it elects the ordinary VAT regime, exceeds the applicable threshold, conducts intra-Community or import transactions, or falls within a special regime. A non-established business generally has no equivalent broad domestic threshold and may require French VAT registration from its first taxable French transaction, subject to place-of-supply and special-regime rules. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies principally to qualifying intra-Community distance sales and certain electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronic services to EU consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction reporting through approved private platforms or the public invoicing platform framework. All French-established businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026. Large enterprises and tax groups must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; small and medium-sized enterprises must generally issue them from 1 September 2027. E-reporting applies to specified B2C and cross-border transactions. France does not generally operate a universal real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping model for ordinary VAT invoices. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. Invoices must contain mandatory French VAT particulars, and electronic records must preserve authenticity, integrity, legibility, auditability, and prescribed retention periods. Customs declarations use the French/EU electronic customs systems, including export declaration and exit-confirmation data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the EU may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct, functionally equivalent to zero-rating, if the supplier acts as exporter or exports through an authorized intermediary and can prove that the goods left the EU customs territory. The supplier must retain the export declaration reference, customs exit confirmation, transport evidence, commercial documentation, and accounting records. Intra-Community supplies to a VAT-identified customer in another EU Member State are exempt only if the statutory customer-identification, transport, recapitulative-statement, and evidentiary conditions are satisfied. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France are generally outside the scope of French VAT under place-of-supply rules rather than technically zero-rated; exceptions apply to services connected with French immovable property, passenger transport, events, short-term vehicle hire, and other special categories. Export VAT refunds require a recoverable input-VAT position, valid invoices, business-use substantiation, and compliance with the applicable VAT return or refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export declaration submitted through the competent customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs release-for-export data and electronic confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Transport document, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier proof, or equivalent multimodal document
Packing list and product-level shipment records where relevant
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery evidence, and proof of consignee or destination outside the EU
Accounting and VAT return records reconciling the export to the zero-rated or exempt turnover
Inward remittance or bank evidence where commercially available; France does not impose a general universal inward-remittance certificate as a statutory condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export VAT exemption may be denied or clawed back if the supplier cannot prove export, the goods did not leave the EU, documents are inconsistent, the transaction is fictitious, or the customer and transport conditions are not substantiated. The tax administration may reassess unpaid VAT, late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and penalties generally ranging from 10% for certain filing or payment failures to 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres, abuse of law, or concealed activity, subject to statutory facts and procedure. Customs-specific fines, seizure, repayment of customs benefits, and other sanctions may apply independently. Serious VAT fraud can also trigger criminal proceedings, including imprisonment and substantial fines, with aggravated sanctions for organized or fraudulent schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in conjunction with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the supervisory authority for banks and investment firms; the external exchange control and prudential mandate are coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains a fully liberalised foreign exchange regime; the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account transactions. No prior authorisation is required for profit remittance, dividend distributions, or inbound direct investment, except in specifically reserved sensitive sectors (Decree 2019-1590). Capital account operations, including cross-border loans and equity injections, must be reported to the Banque de France for statistical and balance-of-payments purposes when the transaction value exceeds €1,000,000. Profit and dividend remittance is permitted freely through bank channels, pending presentation of customary corporate authorisations, tax compliance certificates, and anti-money laundering documentation. For botulinum toxin manufacturing (ISIC 2100), the pharmaceutical sector is not automatically classified as a sensitive foreign investment field unless it implicates 'essential interests' (e.g., dual-use or biosecurity concerns).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may maintain foreign currency bank accounts or freely convert repatriated revenue into euros within or outside France. Cross-border export receipts, whether in EUR or foreign currency, trigger declaration obligations to the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) and the Banque de France for balance-of-payments and customs statistical reporting. For third-country exports, electronic customs declarations through DELTA/GÜE are required; no fixed conversion ratio or repatriation timeline is legally imposed. However, prudent treasury practice for a French SAS in the medical aesthetics sector is to repatriate receivables within 90 days and to document all intra-group and third-party trade settlements to support transfer pricing and tax compliance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (and potentially Capital Escrow Account if share capital is paid on a subscription basis)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance Account for Letter of Credit transactions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for the core operational account of a high-risk special-license company. European Economic Area (EEA) electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto or Shine, may onboard the entity for ancillary payment processing only, but they are generally prohibited or risk-averse in accepting regulated pharmaceutical or neurotoxin product lines. Offshore digital EMIs without ACPR or ECB e-money licence are not viable for statutory treasury functions, capital escrow, or trade finance. Legal constraints under the French Monetary and Financial Code and the 5th AML Directive require that any credit institution or EMI performing cross-border settlements on behalf of a high-risk client demonstrate robust transaction monitoring; EMIs routinely decline such relationships. Desirable fintech supplements, not substitutes, include dedicated FX platforms (e.g., forward forward via brokers) and expense management tools, but the primary obligations must flow through a tier-1 regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A face-to-face or video-recognised identity verification is required under French AML/KYC rules (Code monétaire et financier, Art. R561-5). For high-risk sectors (special-license pharmaceutical/biotech), the ACPR expects full at-risk onboarding, which effectively mandates a physical interview of at least one director/responsible person at the bank branch. Remote opening may be possible for low-risk clients through video KYC, but not for botulinum toxin formulation / manufacture. The SAS commercial model, due diligence, and beneficial ownership declaration will necessitate in-person presentation of the original statutory license (ANSM authorisation), ISIC 2100 activity certificate, and a bio-ethics compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector red flag — manufacture of a neurotoxin that can be considered a potential dual-use item or biosecurity subject.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ANSM (French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products) manufacturing license; EMA (European Medicines Agency) transparency or GMP certificate; end-user certificate for all distribution channels; compliance program under EU Dual-Use Regulation (EC) 428/2009; evidence of already-completed national export controls screenings and product classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership — non-resident beneficial owners and multi-tier holding structure typical of an SAS promoted by non-EU investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate charters and certificate of incorporation; full register of beneficial owners with shareholding percentages; tax residency certificates from each jurisdiction; source of funds documentation with mandatory declaration of the capital injection into the French SAS; explanation of the economic rationale for the French entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity to international distributors, clinics, and cold-chain logistics providers in jurisdictions that may present money-laundering or healthcare fraud exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Host of signed sales contracts with professional counterparties (clinics, wholesalers, licensed distributors); written anti-fraud due diligence performed on each material customer; cold-chain monitoring Dossier (temperature logs, shipment releases); export licences for each batch where required; supplier invoices for lyophilization and fermentation partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments involving Russia, Middle East, and Asia-based dermatology clinics that could trigger targeted sanctions or asset-freeze lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full digital compliance screening of every counterparty against EU/AFIN/UK sanctions lists; incorporation certificates and articles of association of each counterparty; bank confirmation of clearance from OFAC- and EU-administered sanctions; receipts of fee payments to registered anti-money laundering consultants; a written policy for rejecting any transaction linked to sanctioned persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols for receiving share capital or shareholder deposits into France: SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR injections (USD, GBP, CHF, or CNY) or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR transfers from an EU shareholder. All inbound foreign direct investment must be reported to the Banque de France under the balance-of-payments survey (Filier S01 'direct investment') within 5 business days if the amount exceeds €1,000,000. The receiving bank will require a corporate authorisation document, bank account certificate, and an anti-money laundering source-of-funds questionnaire, and will validate the purpose code (e.g., S01 for share capital, S13 for shareholder loans). For other global inbound transfers, a copy of the valid passport/director identification, notarised corporate resolution, and tax clearance proof are mandatory. No prior administrative authorisation is required except in sensitive sectors as noted in the FX regime section.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements must be selected according to currency and destination. For EUR disbursements within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), use SEPA Credit Transfers via TARGET2; for non-EUR disbursements (USD, GBP, AED, CNY), use SWIFT MT103 with a beneficiary bank of confirmed standing. For pharmaceutical raw materials or active substances procured from third-country counterparties, bankers' documentary letters of credit (DC / LC) under UCP 600 are mandatory to protect both parties and to evidence shipping conditions, especially when temperature-controlled logistics are required. Use irrevocable conformed LCs when transacting with new or high-risk jurisdictions. The treasury team must attach a casting of commercial invoices, packing lists, and the EU export license for the active substance. Real-time gross settlement (RTGS) through Target 2 or T2 is appropriate for large-value transfers above the THRESHOLD in EUR. Banks may require a written mandate for all wire instructions executed over SWIFT; for cold-chain disbursements, a pre-cleared beneficiary list should be maintained to accelerate checks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Currency Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for coverage of commercial receipts and payments up to 1 year
FX Swaps (FX swap plain vanilla) for short-term liquidity management between EUR and foreign currency
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for shareholder loans or project finance in foreign currencies
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted solely when an underlying exposure exists in a non-convertible or restricted-access currency, with contemplated delivery in EUR at expiry
Currency Options (zero-cost collars) for hedging contingent foreign exchange exposure arising from foreign acquisitions or tenders

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation and update of Ultimate Beneficial Owners in the commercial register, with changes notified within one month

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 25%, plus 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax where annual turnover exceeds EUR 7.63 million (combined marginal burden approximately 25.825%). Qualifying SMEs may benefit from 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit. R&D tax credit (CIR) 30% on eligible expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that ceiling; SME innovation tax credit (CII) 20% on eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; young innovative company (JEI) exemption available for approved high-R&D SMEs. Tax losses carry forward indefinitely, with annual utilization capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of remaining taxable income above that amount.
